archetype.name: Pocket Passer (play-action timing)
archetype.definition: A rhythm thrower who wins from structure in Kyle Shanahan's under-center, play-action offense: accurate, decisive in the middle of the field, rarely sacked, and most dangerous when his best receivers are on the field to turn completions into chunks.

report.headline: Top-five efficiency built on Evans and play-action; the post-bye health check decides everything
report.take:
Purdy is what he has been for most of his career: a high-completion, high-efficiency operator in an offense built to make the quarterback's reads clean. His 0.29 EPA per dropback ranks 5th of 47, his CPOE sits 5.5 points above the league average, and that profile matches 2023 (1st in EPA per play) and 2025 (6th). None of this is a hot start out of nowhere. It is the same player, slightly more aggressive downfield, averaging 8.28 yards an attempt against a league norm of 6.99.

The engine is the structure around him. Under center he completes 79.4% with a 16.9 CPOE. From shotgun his CPOE is -0.9. The middle of the field returns 0.581 EPA per attempt. Those are play-action and timing windows. The other engine is Mike Evans: 1.023 EPA per target on 40 targets, far more value than any other receiver. Kittle (0.349) is steady. McCaffrey's 42 targets return only 0.034 a target, and throws behind the line are a drain at -0.319 per play. When the ball goes vertical to Evans the offense runs at a top-two level. When it gets dumped to the backfield it doesn't.

The last three games show what happens when that support thins out. From Week 5 to Week 7 his EPA per dropback fell to 0.035, roughly league average. His sack rate doubled to 6.7%, his TD rate dropped to 4.1%, and he threw three picks. Two of those three defenses (Seattle, Atlanta) now rank top-eight, and Seattle pressured him on 35.3% of dropbacks. Evans, Samuel and McCaffrey all ended that stretch on the injury report. His CPOE in that stretch (4.4) barely moved, so the accuracy held. The explosiveness and the cushion behind it are what disappeared. That points to circumstance rather than decline.

Some numbers will cool regardless. Eleven red-zone touchdowns without an interception on an 18.8 CPOE, and 0.902 EPA on just 18 deep attempts, are hot small samples. Third down (-5 CPOE) is a real soft spot. The baseline is still a top-ten passer, and the bye plus a soft Raiders defense set up a rebound if the receivers come back.

strengths.title: Play-action accuracy from under center
strengths.body: His completion rate and CPOE spike under center, where Shanahan's boot and play-action concepts give him defined reads and open middle-of-the-field windows. It is schematic, but he has produced top-ten CPOE in three of four full-ish seasons, so it holds up.

strengths.title: Sack avoidance that is a career trait
strengths.body: Only 3.2% of dropbacks end in sacks (2nd of 47), and pressure turns into a sack only 17.9% of the time. That matches last year's 5th-ranked pressure-to-sack rate, so it is who he is, helped by a line that allows the third-lowest hit rate. The recent sack spike came against heavy Seattle pressure, not a change in habits.

strengths.title: Scrambles that pay off
strengths.body: He doesn't run designed plays well (1.75 yards a carry), but when the pocket breaks he finds yards. His 15 scrambles averaged 0.909 EPA and produced 9 first downs. This is the release valve that keeps a 3.0-second time to throw from turning into sacks.

concerns.title: Efficiency rides heavily on Evans
concerns.body: Evans' 40 targets have produced 40.9 EPA. No other target comes close, and the receiver room behind him is thin, with Aiyuk out, Stribling on IR until December and Robinson on IR. Without Evans, the volume shifts toward McCaffrey's low-value targets and screens behind the line. That looks a lot like the Week 5 to Week 7 version of this offense.

concerns.title: Three-game slide toward average
concerns.body: Over the last three games his EPA per dropback (0.035) sat right at the league average, with more sacks and interceptions. Opponent quality and receiver injuries explain much of it. Still, his bad-throw rate is up 2.6 points on last year, and his career interception counts have always ranked poorly. The turnover risk is real, not just noise.

concerns.title: Red-zone and third-down extremes
concerns.body: Eleven red-zone touchdowns with no picks on an 18.8 CPOE will not hold over a full season, so his TD rate should come down. Meanwhile third down, where defenses take away the scheme's easy answers, shows a -5 CPOE and near-neutral EPA. That gap between scripted downs and obvious passing downs is the real ceiling on his profile.

trend.note: He was dominant against Miami and Arizona in Weeks 2-3 and solid through Week 4. Then he slid to near-average efficiency against Seattle, Washington and Atlanta as pressure rose and the receiving corps got banged up, with the Atlanta loss bringing two interceptions.

nextGame.headline: Rested, likely reloaded, and facing the league's worst short-pass defense
nextGame.body:
Las Vegas ranks 25th in pass defense EPA and 30th in success rate. It is dead last in EPA allowed on short passes, which is exactly where Purdy's 78.7% completion rate and 7.0 CPOE on 0-9 yard throws live. The Raiders lean on tight ends more than most defenses (29.5% of targets against them go to TEs, versus 23.9% league-wide), a natural lane for Kittle. They have held WR1s below their averages, though, and they hit quarterbacks at the 5th-highest rate. So the Seattle-style pressure problem could show up in spots, even if their sack rate is only middling. As 10-point home favorites with a 51.5 total, the 49ers project to lead, which can mean more running late. He has still been efficient when ahead by two scores.

Availability is the swing. Evans is expected back after the bye, and McCaffrey's hamstring is described as mild with the team expecting him ready. Samuel has a chance, and Robinson may return from IR. Evans' return matters most, because he is the deep and intermediate threat that turns Purdy's accuracy into chunk plays. On the Raiders' side, corner Darien Porter is questionable with a groin injury after leaving their last game. He plays a part-time share, but losing him would further thin a secondary that already gives up yards.

keyMatchups.title: Short-game rhythm vs. a soft underneath zone
keyMatchups.body: His short throws return 0.344 EPA with a 7.0 CPOE, and the Raiders allow the most EPA on short passes in the league. Quick completions should turn into yards after the catch rather than stalled drives.

keyMatchups.title: Kittle against a TE-heavy target funnel
keyMatchups.body: Opponents throw to tight ends against Las Vegas well above the league share. Kittle is already Purdy's most-targeted receiver at 0.349 EPA a target, which fits a game where the Raiders have held WR1s down.

keyMatchups.title: Raiders' QB hits vs. his pocket
keyMatchups.body: Las Vegas ranks 5th in hit rate, and pressure is what sank his Week 5 game. His line ranks 3rd in hit rate allowed, and his pressure-to-sack rate is among the league's best. The protection edge should favor San Francisco, but it is the one place the Raiders can make him uncomfortable.

nextGame.watch: Whether Evans is active and running vertical routes. If he is, expect early-season Purdy. If not, expect lots of Kittle and checkdowns.

restOfSeason.body:
The baseline is sturdy: top-ten CPOE, elite sack avoidance and a top-two offense by EPA and success rate, all consistent with his 2023 and 2025 seasons. Expect efficiency closer to his full-season level than to the last three weeks once the receivers return. Expect volume to stay moderate at around 30 attempts in an offense that runs well and often plays from ahead. What regresses is the red-zone perfection and the deep-ball EPA on a tiny sample. His TD rate should drift down toward something like 1.6 to 2.2 touchdowns a game, and his interception count should creep toward his career norms rather than stay at the early-season low.

The biggest variable is the health of a wide receiver group that is already short-handed. Evans' Achilles tendinitis is the kind of issue that can flare up, and the depth behind him is thin until Stribling's possible December return. A healthy Evans and Samuel keep him a top-five efficiency passer. Another stretch without them looks like Weeks 5-7: accurate but ordinary.
swingFactors: McCaffrey and Samuel back to full roles
Pressure from top defenses like Seattle's

confidence.note: The career profile is stable, but seven games and a recent dip are tangled up with receiver injuries and tough opponents.
